quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol quickly, it builds up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body after that hour.

questions.question: You are passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic. Where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked vehicles on your right. This keeps you away from opening car doors and pedestrians stepping between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center to have more space around you.

questions.question: Your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Looking constantly in the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation best keeps riders together with good spacing?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group of riders to stay close together while giving each rider enough space around them.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should check everything except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check the tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. You do not need to check the paint.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and avoid braking.
Shift your weight to the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and avoid braking.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and stay in a straight line if a tire goes flat. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Slow down and exit the road when it is safe.

questions.question: You can reduce serious injury risk in a crash by wearing:
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection while riding. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield helps protect your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:
questions.explanation: Shift into higher gears as your motorcycle's speed increases.

questions.question: Which one does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: A person's BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol they drink, and how fast they drink it. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Before riding, check the motorcycle clutch. A properly working clutch should feel:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, why does a motorcycle rider have an advantage over a car driver?

options.text: The motorcycle can accelerate faster than a car.
The motorcyclist can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
Motorcycles can stop shorter than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcyclist can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles on your right, you can ride on the left side of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between vehicles. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what is the best riding position?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars in front of you. The left tire track is often best, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: What color and lettering do service signs have?
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: What is a problem with riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You may not be able to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could swerve into your lane or block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: It should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It only takes a few minutes.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's total stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Maintain at least a three-second following distance when riding at night.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should mirrors be used?

options.text: All riders should check mirrors frequently.
Only the lead rider should check mirrors.
Mirrors should not be checked often because they distract riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders should check mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, all riders should check their mirrors often. This helps you watch the riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look far ahead down the road.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead down the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid danger while riding, always look far ahead on the road. This helps you see problems before you reach them and gives you time to react.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed if you wear a helmet.
Is only needed for long rides.
Should be used on every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on every ride.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can hurt your hearing, even with a helmet on. Always wear hearing protection when you ride.

questions.question: Motorcycles may pass on the right:

options.text: If there are at least eight feet of open pavement.
By riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there are at least eight feet of open pavement.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the other vehicle. Never leave the road surface to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: The safest part of a lane:
questions.explanation: The safest lane position changes based on road and traffic conditions. Move your position in the lane as needed for safety.

questions.question: Motorcycle helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time you ride a motorcycle.
